checks: Each high upper endpoint is at least 1/2+t and each low lower endpoint is at most -1/2-t. Averaging the two corresponding corners forces both bounds at central base (1,1), so any convex containing set has central length at least 1+2t.

Choose the four intervals as close to zero as allowed. Their four continuous ranges lie in [-1/2-t,1/2+t], and the two extremes are realized as diagonal midpoint values at the center. This proves sharpness. The additionally selected centered middle and edge trims also lie in the same range.
A fixed horizontal radius section of a convex lift is itself convex, so exact central length t is impossible for that slice. This does not constrain constructions that change the level measure.

For homothetic trims about the old corner centroids ±1, the averages force ±(1+t/2) at the central base, giving length at least 2+t. Checked original a1e40e6e6a2316e4 §3 (4), §5 and the final homothetic case in §4.
